headline: US Consumer Confidence Surges to 103.3 in November
summary: The Conference Board’s Consumer Confidence Index rose to 103.3 in November from 91.9 in October. The increase reflects growing optimism among American consumers following the conclusion of the elections and a retreat in gas prices.
why: Consumer confidence is a leading indicator of household spending, which accounts for the majority of US economic activity.

impacts.name: S&P 500
impacts.why: Higher consumer confidence generally supports corporate earnings expectations.
impacts.baseline_rule: first recorded price at or after created_at (15-minute price recorder); end = first price at least 24 h later, within 48 h

why_moved: Improved sentiment is driven by political certainty and lower energy costs, which increase disposable income.
